chunks: My father narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Mattīl, from ‘Imrān ibn Mūsā, from Abū ‘Abdillāh al-Jāmūrānī al-Rāzī, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Alī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Sayf ibn ‘Amīrah, from Sandal, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: No one drinks from the water of the Euphrates and is given a sweetening (of the palate) with it when born, except that he loves us, because the Euphrates is a believing river.

key_terms.يُحَنَّكُ بِهِ: Sweetened with it (a ritual done for newborns)

ai.seo_question: Why is the Euphrates River considered a believer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Ṣādiq’s (a) teaching that the Euphrates is a 'believing river' (nahr mu'min), linking its spiritual purity to the affection of its people for the Ahl al-Bayt. This tradition reflects the Shia eschatological view of the Euphrates as a witness to divine truth, where physical connection to its waters symbolizes an innate spiritual affinity with the Prophet's household.
